target.summary: Fall at home on Oct 19, 2026 with a skin tear to the left forearm; PT recommends a walker and home safety evaluation.

planted.text: Follow-up on the fall from Oct 19, 2026: resolved. Roman is back to his usual baseline and no further follow-up is needed. Removed from the active problem list.

headline: Roman has had several changes this period: a fall on Oct 19, new evening confusion, 8.6% weight loss since Sep 5, and a decline in bathing and dressing ability. The notes also disagree on whether the fall is resolved.

items.statement: On 2026-11-09 his niece Linda reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. He was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The RN planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week. No results or visit are documented in the evidence, and no encounters are recorded.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 11-09 RN note; the empty encounters record supports the statement that no visit or encounters are recorded. No results documented.

items.statement: On 2026-10-19 Roman fell in his kitchen while reaching for a cabinet and was found on the floor by Linda. He denied head strike or loss of consciousness and had a small left forearm skin tear. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: Every detail matches note n001 (fall, kitchen, found by Linda, no head strike or LOC, forearm skin tear, high fall risk, PT referral).

items.statement: The notes conflict about the fall. The PT evaluation on 2026-10-24 found slow, unsteady gait with a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. It recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation, bathroom grab bars and PT twice weekly. A second PT note the same day calls the fall resolved, says he is at baseline, and removes it from the problem list. The team should confirm which is correct.
items.verifier_note: The PT evaluation (TUG 19 s, walker, home safety evaluation, grab bars, twice weekly) and the same-day note calling the fall resolved are both documented. The conflict is accurately described.

items.statement: Weight fell from 82.3 kg on 2026-09-05 to 75.2 kg on 2026-11-24, a loss of 7.1 kg (8.6%). The readings were 79.8 kg on Oct 1 and 77.3 kg on Oct 28. He reports poor appetite, skips breakfast, and eats about 50% of day center lunches. The dietitian's plan is an oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check.
items.verifier_note: The weights, the 7.1 kg loss and 8.6% come from the vitals record, and the dietitian note supports the appetite, lunch and plan details. The dietitian note says 9%, and the brief's 8.6% is the record's figure, so this is not a contradiction. The weekly weights and dental check are supported. Overall the item is mostly supported, but the brief does not flag that the 8.6% differs from the note's rounded 9%. Strictly, all facts are present, so this is a minor point only.

items.statement: On 2026-09-25 OT found he now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing. He was independent at the last review. On Sep 18 he needed hands-on help out of the tub and said he was skipping showers for fear of slipping. OT recommended a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing. The evidence does not show whether these were put in place.
items.verifier_note: The 09-25 OT note supports the moderate assistance, the prior independence and the recommendations. The 09-18 aide note supports the tub help and skipping showers. Neither note says whether the recommendations were implemented, and the brief says as much.

questions: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on Nov 9 completed, and what did they show?
Is the fall resolved (Oct 24 note n016) or still active (PT recommendations in n002)? Should it go back on the problem list?
Have the walker, grab bars, tub transfer bench, handheld shower and home safety evaluation been arranged, and have home care hours increased?
Could the evening confusion, weight loss and functional decline be related, and how should the team assess them together?
What is the interim plan for stove safety and evening supervision at home?
